To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we have proposed an action descriptor based on kinematic primitives that is able to represent the motion of an activity in a frame; (2) the descriptor is based on a multi-level motion representation, which makes it suitable for representing a wide variety of actions; (3) we have shown that our descriptor achieves competitive results in action recognition tasks; (4) we have demonstrated that the proposed method is fast and efficient, and can be used for real-time action recognition.
We present an action descriptor that represents actions instantaneously in each video frame.
the proposed action descriptor is easy to implement and computationally efficient.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a novel approach for action recognition based on the characterization of trajectories and their motion.
the design of novel action descriptors that can be efficiently computed and are robust to different action variations, such as viewpoint and illumination changes, occlusions, etc.
the development of novel methods for the recognition and understanding of human actions in video sequences.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach is a very promising solution for online action recognition, and can be easily implemented and extended to more complex scenarios.
the proposed approach is a very fast and efficient action descriptor that can be used for online action recognition.
the proposed approach achieves a competitive accuracy with a very fast computational time, which is very attractive for real-time applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed a novel action representation that can characterize a wide range of actions in a single video frame.
we propose a novel approach for the representation of motion trajectories for action recognition in videos.
we have introduced a novel action descriptor for video-based human activity recognition that represents activities instantanously in each frame of the video sequence.

the proposed action descriptor can be easily computed and it is robust enough to be applied to a broad range of action recognition tasks.
